verdict.probe_answer: Both arms fix the root cause by collecting parameters and doing one ordered binding pass, then attaching per-param facts by def_byte. Both add an ordinal regression that would fail on the buggy per-param add_locals implementation. Both appear inert for other binding sites; let/pattern callers remain single ordered passes.
verdict.rationale: Arm A is functionally correct: it adds an Option<LocalFact> path so params can attach facts separately, then binds all params in one add_locals call. Its ordinal test would catch the collision, and it adds the required ambiguity-to-None test. Arm B does the same repair but with a cleaner binding-only helper that preserves the existing add_locals API for ordinary call sites. Its tests are stronger: the ordinal pin lives in the name_resolution integration area and the duplicate-local lookup test includes a positive non-vacuity assertion before checking ambiguity. That makes B materially better, though A is also acceptable.
